Minimal PLQR demo data (oracle nuisances; no internal fitting) (experimental)

Source: R/demo-data-plqr.R
plqr_demo_data.Rd

Generates data for a partially linear quantile regression (PLQR) model $$ Q_{\tau}(Y \mid D, U) \;=\; D^{\top}\,\theta_{0} \;+\; g_{0}(U) \, , $$ with a user-chosen design for the nonparametric shape nuisance \(g_{0}\); the demo specializes to \(U = X\). Errors follow an Asymmetric Laplace distribution (ALD) at level \(\tau\), so the conditional \(\tau\)-quantile equals the right-hand side.

Usage

plqr_demo_data(
  n = 300,
  p = 2,
  p_d = 1,
  tau = 0.5,
  sigma = 0.5,
  design = c("linear", "sinusoidal", "bump"),
  seed = NULL,
  x0 = NULL,
  inject = NULL,
  inject_col = c("Y", "g_oracle", "D1", "mD1", "rD1")[1],
  idx_inject = 3L
)

Arguments

n

Integer; sample size.

p

Positive integer number of features in \(X\).

p_d

Integer; dimension of \(D\) (number of partially linear regressors).

tau

Quantile level in \((0,1)\).

sigma

Positive ALD scale for the regression error (larger means noisier \(Y\)).

design

Character; one of "linear", "sinusoidal", "bump" for \(g_{0}\).

seed

Optional integer seed, used locally without changing the caller's RNG state. NULL uses the current stream.

x0

Optional target point in \(\mathbb{R}^{p}\) for localization (defaults to the zero vector).

inject

Optional, one of NULL, "na", "inf"; if provided, inject a single non-finite into inject_col at row idx_inject. Useful for testing runtime guards.

inject_col

Character; which column to corrupt when inject is not NULL. One of "Y", "g_oracle", "D1", "mD1", "rD1".

idx_inject

Integer row index to corrupt (default 3).

Value

A list with:

  • data: a data.frame with columns X1..Xp, D1..Dp_d, Y; oracle nuisances g_oracle (the value of \(g_{0}(X)\)), mD1..mDp_d (components of \(m_{D}(X)\)), residuals rD1..rDp_d (components of \(D - m_{D}(X)\)), and density_oracle, the true conditional density of \(Y\) at the quantile threshold. Because the demo's ALD errors are independent of \((X, D)\) and homoskedastic, this density is constant, \(f(0) = 4\tau(1-\tau)/\sigma\).

  • x0: the target point used.

  • truth: a list with theta_true (length p_d), g_fn(x) and mD_fn(x) closures to evaluate ground truth at new \(X\), and density_fn(v), the error density at signed distance \(v\) from the quantile threshold (density_fn(0) is the density_oracle value).

  • g_x0: the true value \(g_{0}(x_{0})\).

Details

The function also returns the oracle \(m_{D}(U) \equiv \mathbb{E}[D \mid U]\) to build the orthogonal PLQR score $$ \psi(W;\theta) \;=\; (\tau - \mathbf{1}\{\,Y \le D^{\top}\theta + g_{0}(U)\,\})\, (D - m_{D}(U))\, . $$

Lifecycle

Experimental. The PLQR API and inference interfaces may change.

Examples

demo <- plqr_demo_data(
  n = 300, p = 2, p_d = 1, tau = 0.5,
  design = "sinusoidal", seed = 1
)
